blocks.text: I can appreciate that a sequence is a succession of terms usually formed according to a rule.
A sequence does not have to be made of numbers. It can be made of patterns of objects, and we can describe how the pattern grows.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A sequence is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule.
Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a term.

blocks.text: A sequence can be made from a pattern of objects. To draw the next pattern, we first have to understand how the pattern develops.
Imagine a pattern made of white squares in the middle with black squares around the edge. Three pupils each say “each pattern increases by…”.

items.title: Increases by 1
items.sub: the white squares in the middle, or the width

items.title: Increases by 2
items.sub: the black squares around the edge, or the perimeter

items.title: Increases by 3
items.sub: all the squares together, or the area

blocks.text: They can all be right! It depends which part of the pattern each person is talking about.
We can look at individual parts of a pattern to describe how it develops. It is important to be precise about which object we mean.

House pattern: the first pattern is one house made of 3 solid red lines and 2 dashed blue lines. Each new house adds 2 red lines and 2 blue lines, because one red line is already there from the last house. The height stays the same.

items: Red lines: 2 for each house, plus 1 extra at the start.
The 4th pattern has 9 red lines and 8 blue lines.

blocks.label: Total lines for 4 houses?
blocks.text: 9 red + 8 blue = 17 lines. It is not 20: only the first house needs 3 red lines.
Same house pattern: 3 red and 2 blue lines for one house, then 2 more red and 2 more blue for each new house.

items.q: How many red lines for 6 houses?
How many blue dashed lines for 6 houses?
How many lines altogether for 6 houses?
A pattern has 41 red lines. How many blue dashed lines does it have?

blocks.text: Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a {term}. In a pictorial sequence each pattern is a term: term 1, term 2, term 3, …
Here is a pattern with white squares in the middle and black squares around them. Term 1 has 8 black squares. Every new term adds 1 white square and 2 black squares.

items: Compare with the previous term: the black squares increase by 2 from one term to the next.
Compare the objects: the number of white squares is the term number. Term 10 has 10 white squares.
2 black squares for each white square, plus 3 at each end (6 in all): black = white × 2 + 6.

blocks.text: Use the pattern from the last slide: black squares = 2 × (white squares) + 6, and term 1 has 8 black squares.

items.q: How many black squares are in term 10?
How many black squares are in term 15?
A term has 20 white squares. How many black squares does it have?

blocks.text: It can help to write the number of a certain object in each pattern. Then you can see the rule more easily.

items: Count the lines in each pattern: 3, 9, 15, … Each term adds 6 lines, so term 4 has 21 lines.
Count the perimeter of each pattern: 3, 6, 9, 12, … The perimeter increases by 3 each term. The term number × 3 gives the perimeter.

blocks.text: Counting the same object in every term turns a pattern of pictures into a number sequence.
A pictorial sequence has 3, 9, 15 lines in terms 1, 2, 3, with a constant additive pattern. Its perimeters are 3, 6, 9, 12, … for terms 1, 2, 3, 4, …

blocks.q: How many lines are there in term 5?
What is the perimeter of term 8?
blocks.why: The perimeter is the term number × 3, so term 8 has 8 × 3 = 24.

blocks.text: In a school dining hall, 6 chairs fit around one rectangular table. Now the tables are put end to end in a row.

items: Each table has 4 chairs, plus 2 chairs for the ends of the row.
26 chairs are needed for 26 pupils: 4 × 6 + 2 = 26, so 6 tables.

blocks.text: Each extra table adds 4 more chairs. The number of chairs is the number of tables × 4, plus 2.
Tables are in a row, end to end. Each table has 4 chairs, plus 2 for the ends.

items.q: How many chairs fit round 8 tables?
How many chairs fit round 12 tables?
How many tables are needed for 46 chairs?

blocks.text: The whole pattern is made of parts, and each part can grow by a different amount.
In the black and white squares pattern, the white squares go up by 1 and the black squares go up by 2. So all the squares together go up by 1 + 2 = 3 each term.
To describe a sequence well, say which part of the pattern you are counting and how it grows from one term to the next.
In the house pattern, the red lines increase by 2 each term and the blue dashed lines increase by 2 each term.

blocks.q: By how much do all the lines together increase each term?
blocks.why: The red lines go up by 2 and the blue lines go up by 2, so all the lines go up by 2 + 2 = 4.

items: A sequence is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule. Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a term.
A pattern of objects can be made by following a rule, and the rule can be described in words.
Be precise about which object you are describing: white squares, black squares, all the squares, lines, perimeter…
Writing the number of objects in each term as a number sequence helps you spot the rule and find missing terms.

flashcards.front: What is a term in a sequence?
flashcards.back: Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a term.
A sequence is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule.

flashcards.front: In a pictorial sequence, what is each pattern called?
Why must we be precise when we describe how a pattern grows?
flashcards.back: Different parts of a pattern can grow by different amounts, so we must say which object we mean (for example white squares, black squares or the perimeter).

flashcards.front: The white squares in a pattern go up by 1 each term and the black squares by 2. By how much do all the squares go up?
In the house pattern, how many red lines are there for 10 houses?
flashcards.back:
21

Two red lines for each house, plus 1 extra at the start.

flashcards.front: In the house pattern (2 blue lines per house), how many blue lines are there for 10 houses?
A pattern has terms with 3, 9, 15 lines. What is the rule and what is term 4?
flashcards.back: Add 6 lines each term, so term 4 has 21 lines.

flashcards.front: A pattern has a perimeter of 3, 6, 9, 12 in terms 1 to 4. How could you find the perimeter of any term?
In a pattern the number of black squares is white squares × 2 + 6. How many black squares are there in term 10?
Tables in a row, end to end, each with 4 chairs plus 2 for the ends. How many chairs for 4 tables?
Why does it help to write the number of objects in each term as numbers?
flashcards.back: It makes it easier to see the rule for the sequence, and to find missing terms.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Formalising a sequence
worksheet.instructions: Each question describes a pattern that grows by a rule. Work out the numbers in the pattern, then answer with a number.

questions.prompt: House pattern: the first pattern is one house made of 3 red lines and 2 dashed blue lines. Each new house adds 2 red lines and 2 blue lines. How many red lines are there for 12 houses?
questions.explanation: Red lines: 2 for each house plus 1 extra at the start: 2 × 12 + 1 = 25.

questions.prompt: Same house pattern (each house has 2 blue dashed lines). How many blue dashed lines are there for 12 houses?
Same house pattern. How many lines are there altogether for 12 houses?
Same house pattern. A pattern has 41 red lines. How many blue dashed lines does it have?
questions.explanation: There is always one more red line than blue lines, so 41 − 1 = 40.

questions.prompt: A pattern has white squares in the middle and black squares around them. Term 1 has 1 white square and 8 black squares, and every new term adds 1 white square and 2 black squares. How many black squares are in term 15?
questions.explanation: Black squares = 2 × white squares + 6, and term 15 has 15 white squares: 2 × 15 + 6 = 36.

questions.prompt: Same black and white pattern (black squares = 2 × white squares + 6, and term n has n white squares). Which term number has 40 black squares?
A pictorial sequence has 3, 9, 15 lines in terms 1, 2, 3 and carries on with a constant additive pattern. How many lines are there in term 8?
The perimeters of terms 1, 2, 3, 4 of a pattern are 3, 6, 9, 12, and it carries on the same way. What is the perimeter of term 20?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is the term number × 3: 20 × 3 = 60.

questions.prompt: Tables are put end to end in a row. Each table has 4 chairs plus 2 chairs for the ends. How many chairs fit round 8 tables?
Tables are put end to end in a row. Each table has 4 chairs plus 2 chairs for the ends. How many tables are needed for 46 chairs?
